title: Replying to @🔪 Alison ♥️ Foreman ☠️ Here you go! #broadway #theatre #...
transcript: “Stage version of 1984 makes audiences faint, vomit, scream.” And yes, Olivia Wilde was in the Broadway production. This was genuinely one of the most unsettling theater experiences I've ever had. I didn't faint, vomit or scream, but I did see it with three friends from the front row. And let me tell you, we walked out of that theater utterly shaken. Just like, dead silent. This was a stage adaptation of George Orwell's 1984, and was actually a collaboration between two artists who you might recognize from this recent Broadway season: Duncan Macmillan of Every Brilliant Thing and Robert Icke of Oedipus. They both co-wrote it and co-directed it. It started at the Almeida Theatre in London. It went to the West End, where I saw it, and then later to Broadway. And I found it to be a singularly bizarre piece of theater, sometimes deliberately disorienting you from your sense of reality and sometimes just a brutal assault on the senses. In particular, it was the infamous torture scene that was really rough to watch, especially from the front row. just being so close while this actor is screaming, drooling, squirming, covered in bIood. But was the show actually good? I don't know. I really couldn't say. It was kind of a mess. I thought it was really on the nose. But, boy, did it pack a punch. And I can't say that I regret seeing it. In retrospect, though, I wish I had waited to see it on Broadway. So I could see Olivia Wilde. She was the female lead opposite Tom Sturridge. And this was, like, a couple years before Booksmart came out, I think. if anyone saw her in the role, I'd be really curious to know how she was. But either way, I really respect her for being game for such a bizarre theatrical project. And I hope we get her back in the theater world soon, either as an actor or as a writer director.
